questions: Does TrendPullJob carry any @Profile/@ConditionalOnProperty that would exclude it from the default component scan, or is it an unconditional @Component?

Does Spring's actual constructor-resolution algorithm (AutowiredAnnotationBeanPostProcessor.determineCandidateConstructors + the SimpleInstantiationStrategy fallback) really throw for a class with one public + one package-private constructor, or is there a documented fallback that silently picks the public one?

Can EV-001 be reproduced without booting the full app (DB/Redis/etc.), using a bare DefaultListableBeanFactory plus the RC's own compiled class and the exact spring-beans jar version pinned in pom.xml (3.3.5)?

In EscrowService.initiateFund, is milestone.status ever checked anywhere in the call chain (assertContractActiveForMilestone, deriveFundAmount, the controller) before a new EscrowHold is created for a milestoneId that already has one?
Is there a DB-level UNIQUE/CHECK constraint on escrow_holds(milestone_id) or payment_milestones that would prevent two FUNDED holds from ever existing against the same milestone?

When releaseInternal(milestoneId) resolves 'the' hold to release, does it key off milestone.escrowHoldId (which a re-fund silently overwrites) or some invariant that would make a double release structurally impossible?
Is there an existing EscrowServiceTest covering 'fund a milestone that is already FUNDED/RELEASED with a fresh Idempotency-Key'?
In WalletService.requestCreatorWithdrawal/doProcessWithdrawal, is doProcessWithdrawal's own @Transactional a real proxy boundary or a Spring self-invocation no-op?
Does IdempotencyReservationOps.markCompleted commit independently (REQUIRES_NEW) of the ambient transaction that holds the actual wallet debit and the Payout row insert?

Is payoutRepository.save(...) inside doProcessWithdrawal flushed synchronously (so a DB constraint failure surfaces before markCompleted runs), or deferred to the ambient transaction's own commit (so it could fail AFTER markCompleted has already committed)?

Is there a concrete, reachable trigger for a post-action commit failure -- e.g. a VARCHAR-length overflow on the persisted idempotency/reference key -- given what the actual frontend sends as its Idempotency-Key?
Is creator withdrawal (money OUT via RazorpayX) actually reachable in production today, or is it gated behind an FE feature flag and/or an unconfigured/placeholder RazorpayX account?
Does PayoutOrphanedDebitSweepJob's reconciliation sweep cover WalletService's withdrawal path, or only PayoutService's separate queuePayout path?

Are the finders' cited line ranges (TrendPullJob.java:156,175; EscrowService.java:212-341,388-440,473-503; WalletService.java:249-323,381-415; IdempotencyService.java:156-164) accurate against the RC's actual file contents?
For each finding, does the claimed severity survive once reachability/feature-gating in the RC is accounted for?

verdicts.title: TrendPullJob two-constructor Spring boot failure
verdicts.reason: Read TrendPullJob.java in full: it is a plain, unconditional @Component (line 90, no @Profile/@ConditionalOnProperty anywhere on the class) in package com.influora.job, unconditionally caught by @SpringBootApplication's default component scan from InfluoraApiApplication (no exclude filters). It declares exactly two constructors: a public 5-arg one at line 156 and a package-private 7-arg 'test-only seam' at line 175 -- neither carries @Autowired, confirmed exact line match to the finder's citation. Rather than relying on secondhand recollection of Spring's constructor-resolution rules, I built the classpath from the RC's own pom (mvn -o dependency:build-classpath, Spring Boot 3.3.5 / spring-beans 6.1.x) and the RC's own compiled TrendPullJob.class (mvn -o compile), then wrote a standalone probe (kept outside the repo, under my scratchpad, never touching RC source) that: (1) called AutowiredAnnotationBeanPostProcessor.determineCandidateConstructors(TrendPullJob.class, ...) directly -- it returned null, i.e. 'no @Autowired candidates, fall through to default resolution'; (2) registered TrendPullJob as a bean definition on a real DefaultListableBeanFactory with that same real AutowiredAnnotationBeanPostProcessor attached, and called getBean(). Actual result: BeanCreationException wrapping BeanInstantiationException wrapping NoSuchMethodException: com.influora.job.TrendPullJob.<init>() -- message text 'Failed to instantiate [com.influora.job.TrendPullJob]: No default constructor found', matching the finder's claimed error verbatim. This happens because the default-resolution fallback (SimpleInstantiationStrategy.instantiate) looks specifically for a no-arg constructor via clazz.getDeclaredConstructor() with zero arguments, which TrendPullJob does not have. This is a genuine, unconditional, always-reachable context-refresh failure -- it requires no specific profile, env var, or request path; the entire influora-api process cannot start. Confirms the finder's claim at the highest evidence tier this task allows (runtime-reproduced against the RC's own compiled bytecode and exact pinned Spring version, not a toy simulation).
verdicts.new_evidence: Built classpath from RC's own pom (spring-beans 6.1.x / Boot 3.3.5), compiled RC's TrendPullJob.class fresh, and ran a standalone JVM probe against a real Spring DefaultListableBeanFactory: getBean('trendPullJob') threw BeanCreationException -> BeanInstantiationException -> NoSuchMethodException, message 'No default constructor found', reproducing the exact claimed failure outside the toy-hypothesis stage.

verdicts.title: EscrowService.initiateFund can re-fund an already-FUNDED/RELEASED/REFUNDED milestone
verdicts.reason: Traced the full state machine in the RC. initiateFund (213-333, matches the cited 212-341) dedupes ONLY via escrowHoldRepository.findByIdempotencyKey(idempotencyKey) (a client-controlled header) -- a caller supplying a fresh Idempotency-Key for a milestone that already has a FUNDED/RELEASED/REFUNDED hold sails through. The only milestone-related gate for a milestoneId-scoped fund is assertContractActiveForMilestone (388-430, matches the cited 388-440), which checks contract.getBrandSignedAt()/getCreatorSignedAt() and collaboration.getStatus() == CANCELLED -- it never reads milestone.getStatus() (PENDING/FUNDED/RELEASED/REFUNDED/FROZEN, confirmed via MilestoneStatus.java and PaymentMilestone.markFunded at lines 141-145, exact match to the cited PaymentMilestone.java:141-145). EscrowController.fund (the only HTTP entry point) adds no additional milestone-status check either. applyFunding (473-517, matches the cited 473-503) unconditionally calls escrowBackend.fund(...) then milestone.markFunded(hold.getId()) -- this OVERWRITES milestone.escrowHoldId to point at the new hold, orphaning the prior hold (which keeps its own FUNDED/RELEASED status and its own money movement, now unreachable from the milestone). Checked V9__escrow_holds.sql: the only UNIQUE constraint is on idempotency_key; there is no UNIQUE/CHECK on milestone_id, so the DB does not prevent a second row. Traced releaseInternal (848-905): it resolves 'the' hold to release via requireHoldForUpdate(milestone.getEscrowHoldId()) -- i.e. whichever hold is CURRENTLY pointed to, which a re-fund silently redirects to the fresh hold -- so releasing after a re-fund releases the NEW hold (status FUNDED, passes requireStatus) regardless of what happened to the earlier hold, giving the 'releasable twice' effect the claim describes. Grepped EscrowServiceTest.java: no test exercises 'fund an already-FUNDED/RELEASED milestone with a new Idempotency-Key', consistent with this being a genuine, currently-unguarded gap rather than a misread of an existing safeguard. This is a real money-movement defect (double debit + an orphaned but still-FUNDED/RELEASED hold + a release path that can pay out twice), which is P0-grade (financial/data-loss class), so I side with meera-db's P0 over vikram-pay's P1.
verdicts.new_evidence: Independently confirmed no milestone.getStatus() read anywhere in the fund path (service or controller), confirmed V9__escrow_holds.sql has no milestone_id UNIQUE/CHECK constraint, and traced releaseInternal to show it always releases whichever hold milestone.escrowHoldId currently points to -- the exact hold a re-fund silently swaps in.

verdicts.title: Creator withdrawal calls RazorpayX before a durable Payout row exists; idempotency can mark COMPLETED independently of the ambient transaction's commit
verdicts.reason: The mechanism is real and I traced it further than the original claim. doProcessWithdrawal (382-415, matches the cited 381-415) is `protected @Transactional` but is invoked via `this.` from inside requestCreatorWithdrawal's own already-open @Transactional (250-318, within the cited 249-323) through a lambda passed to idempotencyService.executeOnce -- a textbook Spring self-invocation no-op (this exact defect class is independently documented, for a DIFFERENT method, in this same codebase's own IdempotencyReservationOps.java javadoc and PayoutOrphanedDebitSweepJob.java javadoc). So doProcessWithdrawal's ledgerService.post() debit, the RazorpayX call, and payoutRepository.save() all run inside ONE physical transaction owned by requestCreatorWithdrawal. Confirmed IdempotencyService.executeOnce (156-164, exact match to the cited lines): action.get() runs doProcessWithdrawal, and reservationOps.markCompleted(...) is called immediately after IF action.get() returns without throwing -- and IdempotencyReservationOps.markCompleted carries @Transactional(REQUIRES_NEW) through a genuine separate-bean proxy call (confirmed by reading IdempotencyReservationOps.java, which documents this exact REQUIRES_NEW-via-separate-bean pattern in detail for a related bug it already fixed), so it commits durably and independently BEFORE requestCreatorWithdrawal's own ambient transaction ever reaches its commit. Unlike IdempotencyReservationOps.tryReserve, which the team deliberately hardened with saveAndFlush() specifically because a plain save() defers the actual INSERT/constraint-check to commit time, doProcessWithdrawal's payoutRepository.save(Payout.createQueued(...)) is a PLAIN save() -- the same deferred-flush hazard the team already reasoned about and fixed elsewhere was not applied here. I found a concrete, non-hypothetical trigger for a late commit-time failure: payouts.idempotency_key is VARCHAR(64) (V48__payouts.sql:13) and doProcessWithdrawal stores scopedKey = "creator-withdraw:" + userId(26-char ULID) + ":" + <client Idempotency-Key> there -- 44 bytes are consumed before the client's own key is even added, and creator-wallet.tsx's default idempotency key is a full UUID (safeRandomUUID(), 36 chars) -- 44+36=80 > 64, a guaranteed overflow on the FE's own default behavior once this path is live. So the exploit chain is real: RazorpayX gets called and a real payout may be queued at the gateway, then the Payout insert can fail at flush/commit time (after markCompleted has already committed COMPLETED independently), leaving no durable local Payout row and a stuck idempotency key -- and PayoutOrphanedDebitSweepJob's sweep (confirmed by reading its own javadoc) is explicitly built around PayoutService's PENDING-row-created-before-the-gateway-call pattern, not WalletService's create-the-row-after pattern, so it would not catch this specific blind spot. However, I downgrade severity from the claimed P0: src/lib/api.ts's own extensive javadoc-style comment confirms VITE_PAYOUTS_ENABLED defaults to DISABLED in production builds (money-OUT stays off by design, unlike money-IN which Swapnil set to default-enabled), the creator-wallet.tsx withdraw button is `disabled` whenever isMoneyActionBlocked('withdraw') is true, and application.yml's razorpay.payout-account-number defaults to the literal placeholder REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_RAZORPAYX_ACCOUNT. So this defect, while real and fully wired to fire the moment withdrawals are turned on with a real RazorpayX account, is NOT reachable in production today behind the current build/config -- matching swapnil's INFERRED/gated framing more than vikram-pay's P0. I rate it P1 (a genuine go-live blocker for enabling money-OUT, not a live P0 incident right now) and evidence_score 4 rather than 5 since I did not execute a live Spring-transaction test proving the commit-order race end-to-end (no existing test covers this; WalletServiceTest has no case for it).
verdicts.new_evidence: Confirmed payouts.idempotency_key is VARCHAR(64) (V48__payouts.sql:13) and computed that doProcessWithdrawal's stored scopedKey (44 fixed bytes + a UUID-length client key, per creator-wallet.tsx's safeRandomUUID() default) reliably exceeds it -- a concrete overflow trigger, not a hypothetical one. Confirmed payoutRepository.save() in doProcessWithdrawal is a plain save(), not saveAndFlush(), unlike the parallel case (IdempotencyReservationOps.tryReserve) the team already hardened for the identical deferred-flush hazard. Confirmed PAYOUTS_ENABLED defaults false and razorpay.payout-account-number defaults to a placeholder, so this path is currently flag-gated off and not live in production.
